text: Edappadi Karuppa Palaniswami, born on 12 May 1954 in Siluvampalayam, Salem district, Madras State (now Tamil Nadu), is an Indian politician who has served as the current leader of opposition in the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly since May 2021. He was the seventh chief minister of Tamil Nadu from 2017 to 2021 and has been the general secretary of the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) since 28 March 2023. Palaniswami was born to Karuppa Gounder and Thavasiyammal and has two siblings, a brother named Govindraj and a sister named Ranjitham. He is married to Ratha and has a son. After completing his B.Sc. zoology from Sri Vasavi College, he worked in agriculture before entering politics in 1974 as a volunteer in AIADMK. He first won a seat in the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly in 1989 from Edappadi, re-elected in 1991, and lost in 1996. In the 1998 general election, he was elected as a Member of Parliament representing Tiruchengodu, but lost in 1999 and 2004. He contested again from Edappadi in 2006 and lost. He was appointed propaganda secretary in July 2006 and organising secretary in August 2007. He was re-elected from Edappadi in 2011 and served as minister of highways and minor ports in the Jayalalithaa cabinet. From June 2011 to April 2022, he was the district secretary of AIADMK for Salem suburban district. In 2014, he was appointed to the party's disciplinary committee. He was re-elected from Edappadi in 2016 and served as minister of public works in the cabinet. He became chief minister in February 2017 following O. Panneerselvam’s resignation after J. Jayalalithaa’s death in December 2016, and was sworn in on 16 February 2017 with a 32-member cabinet, holding charge of home, prohibition, and excise. In March 2017, he introduced the Kudimaramaththu scheme for restoring minor irrigation tanks and lakes. In May 2017, a high-level committee led by M. Anandakrishnan was formed to reform the Tamil Nadu school education system in response to mandatory NEET exams, and the school syllabus and exam pattern for classes 1 to 12 were revised to match CBSE standards starting in the 2018–19 academic year. In May 2018, police fired on protests against a Vedanta copper plant in Thoothukudi, killing 13 people; the government later ordered the plant’s permanent closure on 28 May 2018. On 15 August 2018, Palaniswami announced a 2% sub-quota in government jobs and State Public Sector Undertakings for medal-winning sportspersons, later increased to 3% on 16 October 2018. His administration was praised for its response to Cyclone Gaja in November 2018. In August 2019, he introduced dedicated patrol vehicles (Amma patrol) for women and children’s security. In the 2019 general election, AIADMK, led by Palaniswami, contested in alliance with the Bharatiya Janata Party and won only one seat. He launched the Yaadhum Oore programme to attract foreign investment and visited the United States, United Kingdom, and United Arab Emirates to promote it. In 2019, new districts—Tenkasi, Kallakurichi, Tirupattur, Ranipet, Chengalpattu, and Mayiladuthurai—were created by carving them from existing districts. On 28 February 2019, he laid the foundation stone for the ₹1,652-crore Athikadavu–Avinashi Groundwater Recharge and Drinking Water Supply Scheme, with work commencing on 25 December 2019. In February 2020, the Kaveri delta region was declared a protected special agriculture zone. In May 2020, the government reserved 7.5% of seats in government medical colleges for students from public schools and announced plans to establish eleven new government medical colleges with 1,650 seats. During the fourth phase of excavations at Keezhadi (2017–18) costing ₹5.5 million (US$65,000), 5,820 artifacts and brick constructions from the Sangam era were unearthed. On 20 July 2020, Palaniswami laid the foundation for the Keezhadi museum in Sivaganga district. Under his governance, Tamil Nadu was ranked among the top states in sustainable development according to the Public Affairs Index in October 2020. During the coronavirus pandemic, the state did not experience negative growth and was ranked as the best-performing big state from 2018 to 2021 by India Today. On 5 January 2021, the government announced that Thaipusam would be a public holiday annually. A leadership dispute between Palaniswami and Panneerselvam began in October 2020 when K. T. Rajenthra Bhalaji tweeted that Palaniswami should be the chief ministerial candidate, and Sellur K. Raju stated that MLAs would elect the chief minister. Panneerselvam later confirmed Palaniswami as the chief ministerial candidate on 7 October 2020. AIADMK lost the 2021 assembly elections, and Palaniswami resigned as chief minister on 6 May 2021. He won the Edappadi seat for the third consecutive time and was elected leader of the opposition in the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly on 10 May 2021. The meeting to choose the leader was inconclusive, with both Palaniswami and Panneerselvam claiming the post, leading to internal party unrest; supporters of Palaniswami argued that his regional performance in western Tamil Nadu justified his leadership, while Panneerselvam’s supporters claimed poor performance in other regions due to his policies. Palaniswami was ultimately elected as leader of the opposition. In June 2022, AIADMK district secretaries and senior members criticized the dual leadership system of Palaniswami and Panneerselvam. Palaniswami pushed for the appointment as general secretary ahead of the general council meeting on 23 June 2022, asserting that Panneerselvam ceased to be party coordinator due to unrecognised bylaw amendments. On 11 July 2022, the general council abolished the dual leadership, appointed Palaniswami as interim chief, and expelled Panneerselvam and his loyalists for "anti-party" activities. The Madras High Court nullified these decisions on 17 August 2022, but a division bench upheld them on 2 September 2022, and the Supreme Court of India upheld the latter order on 23 February 2023, confirming Palaniswami’s leadership. On 28 March 2023, AIADMK officially elected Palaniswami as general secretary, and on 20 April 2023, the Election Commission of India recognized him as general secretary, acknowledging the constitutional amendments and changes to office-bearers. On 20 August 2023, a conference was held in Madurai to mark the Golden Jubilee of AIADMK’s founding. On 25 September 2023, Palaniswami led AIADMK to officially leave the National Democratic Alliance ahead of the 2024 general election. After the 2023 Chennai floods, Palaniswami demanded that the chief minister release a white paper on stormwater drain work and criticized the state government for lack of preparedness. In the 2024 general election, Palaniswami led AIADMK in an alliance with Desiya Murpokku Dravida Kazhagam, Puthiya Tamilagam, and the Social Democratic Party of India, contesting 36 seats in Tamil Nadu and one each in Puducherry and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, failing to win any seats. Since 5 July 2025, Palaniswami has been placed under Z+ scale security by the Ministry of Home Affairs due to bomb threats. Ahead of the 2026 Tamil Nadu Assembly elections, he launched the Makkalai Kaappom, Thamizhagathai Meetpom (Let us protect the people and reclaim Tamil Nadu) campaign tour, covering all 234 constituencies in phases, beginning in Mettupalayam, Coimbatore, on 7 July 2025.
